entries.name: bridge_deck

entries.name: routing_walkway_after
entries.note: after: the service walkway opens along the route: grated deck, orange hazard edges, ink posts. Walkable

entries.name: routing_core_after

entries.name: routing_beacon_after
entries.note: after: the beacon steady mint, no halo (levels.md 13)

entries.name: routing_ports_after

entries.name: routing_panel_open

entries.name: payroll_keypad_off

entries.name: bridge_span_retracted
entries.note: the glass bridge's span, 4 x 2 (level 12: the first completed batch extends the bridge toward Mira's chute). retracted: a deck tile at each end and an open trussed pit between them with a cobalt conduit below; the two middle columns block. Orange hazard stripes on both long edges; add `bridge_rail` entries along them

entries.name: bridge_span_extended
entries.note: the glass bridge's span, 4 x 2 (level 12: the first completed batch extends the bridge toward Mira's chute). extended: deck from end to end, all cells walkable. Orange hazard stripes on both long edges; add `bridge_rail` entries along them

entries.name: refund_sign_red
entries.note: the refund sign of level 13, a 24 x 14 wall plate. red: a safety-orange plate with a plus, the ledger turned a refund into a charge. Systems has no pure red or green: red is the orange trim ramp, green the mint circuit ramp; the glyph carries the meaning. Place on the north wall face (the plain wall already blocks)

entries.name: refund_sign_green
entries.note: the refund sign of level 13, a 24 x 14 wall plate. green: a mint plate with a minus, the sign restored. Systems has no pure red or green: red is the orange trim ramp, green the mint circuit ramp; the glyph carries the meaning. Place on the north wall face (the plain wall already blocks)

entries.name: calc_display_charge
entries.note: the inset calculator display of level 13, 2 x 1: a steel desk top with a display sunk into it and an open ledger beside it. charge: '+85' in orange, the ledger marked with an orange plus

entries.name: calc_display_refund
entries.note: the inset calculator display of level 13, 2 x 1: a steel desk top with a display sunk into it and an open ledger beside it. refund: '-85' in mint, the ledger marked with a mint minus

entries.name: alarm_strip_merged
entries.note: the alarm hall strip of level 14, a 64 x 18 wall overlay: six lamps above six porcelain label plates. merged: six identical cobalt lamps over blank plates (Pace lost the labels, two alerts look the same)

entries.name: alarm_strip_separated

entries.name: alarm_strip_muted

entries.name: bridge_shutter_open

entries.name: formula_wall_dark

entries.name: courier_chute_ready

entries.name: mira_decor_signed_sent

entries.name: mira_decor_relay

entries.name: elevator_closed
entries.note: elevator, doors shut: two steel leaves meet at a centre seam, a casing with two lamps, a lit floor indicator, a lit LIFT mat in front. Orientation's module in the systems ramps (shared_pieces.elevator_doors): 3 x 3 cells, rows 0-1 are the north wall, row 2 the lit mat. Replaces three wall_n_plain columns

entries.name: elevator_half
entries.note: elevator, leaves slid 6 px into the jamb pockets: the warm cab shows between them. Orientation's module in the systems ramps (shared_pieces.elevator_doors): 3 x 3 cells, rows 0-1 are the north wall, row 2 the lit mat. Replaces three wall_n_plain columns

entries.name: elevator_open
entries.note: elevator, leaves fully in the pockets (11 px, a 1 px lip stays): the cab is open and the centre cell walks in. Orientation's module in the systems ramps (shared_pieces.elevator_doors): 3 x 3 cells, rows 0-1 are the north wall, row 2 the lit mat. Replaces three wall_n_plain columns

entries.name: elevator_call_panel
entries.note: wall call panel for the elevator, systems ramps (shared_pieces.elevator_call_panel): steel plate, small lit display, up and down buttons. Overlay on wall_n_plain (no collision of its own); place it on the wall face 9 px below the wall top, one cell beside the elevator

entries.name: desk_a_front

entries.name: desk_b_front

entries.name: artifact_id_envelope

No collision: lay it on a desk, a table or a blocked cell

entries.name: artifact_alarm_strip
entries.note: Alarm strip (Systems level 14): a paper strip of six alert pictograms with one extra department mark. 16 x 16 px with a baked contact shadow and a small pale glass-step glint at the upper left as the inspectable cue (never a UI marker colour). No collision: lay it on a desk, a table or a blocked cell

entries.name: artifact_scoring_proof
entries.note: Scoring proof (Systems level 15): a proof sheet with three rising bars (a longer route scores higher). 16 x 16 px with a baked contact shadow and a small pale glass-step glint at the upper left as the inspectable cue (never a UI marker colour). No collision: lay it on a desk, a table or a blocked cell

entries.name: artifact_original_routing_diagram
entries.note: Original routing diagram (Systems level 16): a diagram of nodes and traces with three signatures. 16 x 16 px with a baked contact shadow and a small pale glass-step glint at the upper left as the inspectable cue (never a UI marker colour). entries.name: routing_node_lit

entries.name: refund_ledger_refund

entries.name: folding_stool
entries.note: Hal's folding stool, the same sprite as hal-props-atlas.json stool_folding (imported from hal_sprites.py), seat open, for him to sit on at the end of level 13. 16 x 10 px, footprint 1 x 1 whose top-left is 6 px above the sprite, anchor [8, 10] (the footprint's bottom centre). Hal's seat offset depends on this geometry: seated Hal's anchor (8, 24) lands on the anchor (8, 16) of the stool's cell, so the sprite's top-left sits at (0, 14) in Hal's 16 x 24 frame (hal-atlas.json stool_sprite_in_frame_px). Do not change it here

entries.name: folding_stool_open
entries.note: state `open` of the folding_stool set: identical to folding_stool (Hal's stool_folding), seat open

entries.name: folding_stool_folded
entries.note: state `folded` of the folding_stool set: the stool packed up, legs and seat in one narrow bundle, ink-ramp steel and canvas like Hal's. Same 16 x 10 box, footprint, collision, anchor [8, 10] and layer as the open stool, so the swap never shifts a pixel

service_door.note: play forward on approach, backward on leave; the same frames as Orientation's door, recoloured

lamp.note: glow states: off, on (steady), pulse (wider ring). Wake = off -> on; idle breathing = on <-> pulse.

payroll_keypad.note: level 12: each correct digit lights its node and progress light; off, half (five digits), lit (ten). Light individual conduits with the conduit_* state sets

bridge_span.note: level 12: the first completed payroll batch extends the bridge; retracted blocks the two middle columns, extended is walkable. Rails stay as bridge_rail entries

refund_sign.note: level 13: the refund sign flips to green when the minus is restored (orange plate with a plus, then mint plate with a minus)

calc_display.note: level 13: the inset calculator display reverses from a charge to a refund

alarm_strip.note: level 14: correct labels separate the alarms into six hues and pictograms; muted is the Quiet Alarm side quest

bridge_shutter.note: level 15: the bridge shutters open; place one per window

formula_wall.note: level 15: as clauses become valid the connected parts of the formula illuminate (dark, half, lit). Wave 2 adds the level data's names: dim (same pixels as dark) and clause_1 to clause_6 (the first k boxes lit; clause_6 has the same pixels as lit), so one clause lights at a time

courier_chute.note: Mira's chute: ready while she has a route to offer

elevator.note: play forward on approach or arrival, backward on leave; only open lets the centre cell through (the same set as Orientation's, in the district ramps)

routing_node.note: level 12: one lamp per correct digit; place ten and switch each on its own

refund_ledger.note: level 13: the ledger turns the charge into a refund, orange to mint

alarm_board.note: level 14: each correct label restores one pictogram and its hue; six labels, six states after blank

folding_stool.note: level 13: the stool stands folded, then Hal opens it to sit; same geometry in both states (Hal's seat offset depends on it)

routing_machine.note: Systems landmark: the large routing machine. Every part is a full-size sprite registered at one footprint origin, so a state is a list of parts; place them all at the same cell. The body carries the collision (6x4 cells); the stubs and walkway are floor markings; the other parts are small quest-state overlays. Wave 2 intermediate states (no new pixels, registered parts only): after_12 = nodes and stubs lit; after_13 = after_12 plus the beacon steady; after_14 = after_13 plus the ports lit; the dome core, walkway and open panel arrive with `after` at level 16.
changes_after: the ten routing nodes on the face light up (levels.md 12: ten individually lit routing nodes)
the dome core lights every circuit trace in its conduit family: mint, cobalt and orange (levels.md 16: the machine lights in an intelligible sequence)
the warning beacon steadies from orange with a halo to calm mint (levels.md 13: the machine's warning light steadies)
the port nozzles, the orange riser and the two floor conduit stubs switch from dull to lit (levels.md 12, 16: each correct node lights a conduit)
a grated service walkway with orange hazard edges opens along the route (levels.md 16: a service walkway opens)
the false panel drops open and reveals the Night Shift elevator stop (levels.md 16: Hal pulls down a false panel)
all four lamps switch from the steady glow to the wider pulse glow
